text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 22: On synthetic aggregates with a known answer, rung 7b's model fits 0.96 times the solar capacity with no battery and 1.98 times with a 200 MW battery, for a 25 MW solar half and a real demand-like half'
text.tspan: Figure 22: On synthetic aggregates with a known answer, rung 7b's model
fits 0.96 times the solar capacity with no battery and 1.98 times with a
200 MW battery, for a 25 MW solar half and a real demand-like half

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Each aggregate is a solar half, a battery half, and a demand-like half (2__BEDGE001, V__NFLEX003, 2__ABGAS000, real or as its calendar replica, scaled to a 50 MW 99th percentile), fitted with four fleet curves, a seasonal calendar baseline, and a battery of the assumed power. Each point is the mean over 16 aggregates (4 solar sets by 4 batteries). In the upper panels the black line at 1 is the same model fitted to the solar half alone. The lone dots at True are the fits given the battery half's own power (75 MW for the 25 MW solar half, 50 MW for the 50 MW one).'
text.tspan: Each aggregate is a solar half, a battery half, and a demand-like half (2__BEDGE001, V__NFLEX003, 2__ABGAS000, real
or as its calendar replica, scaled to a 50 MW 99th percentile), fitted with four fleet curves, a seasonal calendar
baseline, and a battery of the assumed power. Each point is the mean over 16 aggregates (4 solar sets by 4
batteries). In the upper panels the black line at 1 is the same model fitted to the solar half alone. The lone dots
at True are the fits given the battery half's own power (75 MW for the 25 MW solar half, 50 MW for the 50 MW one).
